$schema_note: One row per category in cpp_compliance_report.json (63 real categories, excluding _summary). disposition: RPC (remotely reachable via the Pkcs11V32 mirror) | N/A-local (inherently in-process, no network analogue) | SUITE-GAP (function untouched by either local compliance harness). case_ids reference either an acceptance-crate three-transport parity test (v32_parity::vNN_...) or a core-crate unit test (core::fn_name) that exercises the RPC(s) this category maps to. An empty case_ids array with disposition RPC means: the underlying verb(s) are implemented, wired, and proven correct for OTHER mechanisms/algorithms in the same generic RPC family, but this specific category was not the target of a dedicated case — never silently implied as tested when it wasn't. Two RPCs on the Pkcs11V32 service — SplitKey/JoinKey (G2 gap-remediation, 2026-08-26) — are VENDOR EXTENSIONS, not part of pkcs11f.h: they mirror softhsmrustv3::native::split/join (the same calls behind KMIP 3.0 §6.1.12/§6.1.33 Create/Join Split Key) since the engine has no CKM_PQCTODAY_SPLIT_KEY C_* dispatch arm to mirror instead. The ratchet's check (c) only scans for rpc C_*(...) declarations, so these two are invisible to it by design (they cannot regress a pkcs11f.h coverage count they were never part of) — the SplitKey row below documents them anyway, for the same reason every other row exists: so a real capability can never silently drop out of scope.
generated_after_workstream: RW5 (built during RW-T, the program's terminal workstream)

pkcs11f_h_function_count.not_mirrored_justification: All five are N/A-local, not gaps: C_Initialize/C_Finalize are server-process bootstrap lifecycle with no per-request network analogue (see the 'Init' row below); C_GetFunctionList/C_GetInterface/C_GetInterfaceList return function-pointer tables, which are meaningless over a wire — a remote client cannot call through a returned pointer. None of the five map to a named category in cpp_compliance_report.json, so they have no row in `rows` below; documented here instead so the ratchet's silence about them is a deliberate, checked design choice rather than an oversight.

AES-CTR.justification: CK_AES_CTR_PARAMS (pointer-free) via the new cipher_params::aes_ctr RW-P builder (G3, 2026-08-26) — StructBuilder::set_bytes, the first builder to need a fixed-size inline field. Encrypt/decrypt round trip proven in core; V27 proves KAT-grade byte-identical ciphertext across all three transports via the new oneof variant. AES-CBC (raw 16-byte IV) and AES-CBC-PAD are also exercised in the same core test (no dedicated ledger category exists for CBC).

Attributes.justification: C_GetAttributeValue/C_SetAttributeValue with real §5.7.5 consolidated codes (SENSITIVE > TYPE_INVALID > BUFFER_TOO_SMALL); C_DestroyObject (destructive-gated) cased in v6.

AuthWrap.justification: C_WrapKeyAuthenticated/C_UnwrapKeyAuthenticated, restricted by this engine to CKM_AES_GCM, proven via the real CKR_MECHANISM_INVALID rejection for a non-GCM mechanism (RW4) AND the full authenticated-wrap positive round trip — the compliance suite's own NIST_SP800_38D_KAT check — closed in G1 gap-remediation via the CK_GCM_PARAMS RW-P builder: unwrapped key material equals the original, and a tampered AAD is rejected. Wrapped bytes proven byte-identical across all three transports.

BIP32.justification: CKM_BIP32_MASTER_DERIVE via C_DeriveKey — the engine reads its curve from the OUTPUT TEMPLATE's CKA_EC_PARAMS (no CK_*_PARAMS struct at all, confirmed by reading the dispatch arm directly), over a generic-secret 'seed' base key. Proven to produce a real 32-byte EC private key. G3, 2026-08-26.

ChaCha20.justification: CKM_CHACHA20_POLY1305 (the mechanism this category's own compliance-report entry actually observes — a 16-byte MAC tag on C_Encrypt output, which only the Poly1305 AEAD variant produces; plain CKM_CHACHA20 has none) via the new cipher_params::chacha20_poly1305 RW-P builder (G3, 2026-08-26). Round trip proven in core; V27 proves KAT-grade byte-identical ciphertext across all three transports.

CkaIdRetrieval.justification: C_CreateObject, C_FindObjectsInit/C_FindObjects/C_FindObjectsFinal, C_CopyObject, C_GetObjectSize — generic template search; CKA_ID specifically not the case's search key, but the same FSM.

Classical.justification: RSA-PKCS raw sign/verify (CKM_RSA_PKCS, no parameter) over a 2048-bit keypair, plus the positive C_SignRecover/C_VerifyRecover round trip (§5.13, RSA-only — RW6a proved the non-RSA rejection; this is the positive half an RSA key makes possible). G3, 2026-08-26.

DSA.justification: Same generic sign/verify path as Classical — proven via the same RSA-PKCS raw sign/verify case (DSA itself is not a mechanism this engine implements; the category name maps to the generic classical-signature path, already exercised).

DSA-CTX.justification: CK_SIGN_ADDITIONAL_CONTEXT via the new sign_params::additional_context RW-P builder (G3, 2026-08-26) — ML-DSA sign/verify with a context string and CKH_DETERMINISTIC_REQUIRED hedge. Proven in core: same key+msg+context reproduces the identical signature (real determinism), and a mismatched context at Verify time is rejected (context is bound into what's signed). V27 proves KAT-grade byte-identical signatures across all three transports.

ECDH.justification: CKM_ECDH1_DERIVE via C_DeriveKey (RW4, real P-256 keygen + CKA_EC_POINT exchange) and via C_Encapsulate/DecapsulateKey's ECDH-as-KEM path (RW5).

ECDSA.justification: CKM_ECDSA raw (pre-hashed, no parameter, single-part-only) sign/verify over a P-256 keypair. G3, 2026-08-26.

EdDSA.justification: CKM_EDDSA (pure Ed25519, no parameter) sign/verify over an Ed25519 keypair (CKM_EC_EDWARDS_KEY_PAIR_GEN). G3, 2026-08-26.

ErrCodes.justification: ck_rv is a response FIELD on every RPC (design-level, not per-category) — every negative-path case across V1-V21 asserts exact CKR codes, never hardcoded, always captured from an in-process control.

FIPS.justification: Partial per the master plan (§3): self-test/POST surface where exposed is RPC-reachable via the same generic verbs; process-startup aspects are N/A-local. Not separately cased.

Fork.justification: fork(2) semantics cannot exist across a network boundary (master plan §3). The category's intent — independent clients' RNG does not share state — has a real remote analogue (two sessions' C_GenerateRandom draws must differ) but was not built as its own dedicated case; core::random_and_seed_codes_are_the_engines_own asserts two C_GenerateRandom/C_SeedRandom draws differ within one session, not cross-session.

G-DA-X.justification: CKM_SHA3_256 digest (via the generic C_DigestInit/C_Digest/C_DigestUpdate/C_DigestFinal FSM), one-shot and Update/Final proven to agree, plus CKM_KMAC_128 default-params sign (via the generic C_SignInit/C_Sign) on a generic-secret key. G3, 2026-08-26.

G1Security.justification: Partial per master plan §3: sensitive-attribute blocking and login gating are RPC-assertable (cased); process/memory isolation aspects are N/A-local.

G2ChaCha20.justification: Same case and same correction as ChaCha20 — keygen (CKK_CHACHA20 via CKM_CHACHA20_KEY_GEN) and the Poly1305 round trip this category's own compliance entries (Keygen_KeyType/Keygen_GenMech/ Encrypt/RoundTrip) describe.

G2Derive.justification: C_DeriveKey across CONCATENATE_BASE_AND_KEY, SHA256_KEY_DERIVATION, HKDF, PBKDF2, SP800-108 counter+feedback.

G2MechTable.justification: Same as Discovery — mechanism table flags/ranges.

G3Keygen.justification: The real CKR_TEMPLATE_INCONSISTENT (mismatched key-type) and CKR_TEMPLATE_INCOMPLETE (missing CKA_PARAMETER_SET) codes, asserted three ways.

G4Retcodes.justification: Same design-level guarantee as ErrCodes — not separately cased beyond what ErrCodes already lists.

G7Sha3Rsa.justification: Same generic digest/sign path as G-DA-X/SHA-3 and Classical/GapClassical — both halves (SHA3-256 digest, RSA-PKCS sign) now have real case_ids; not separately cased as a combined SHA3+RSA cell.

G8Dual.justification: C_DigestEncryptUpdate proven byte-identical to running Digest+Encrypt as separate FSMs, three ways; C_DecryptDigestUpdate/C_SignEncryptUpdate/C_DecryptVerifyUpdate wired the same way (core case), not separately byte-verified.

GAsync.justification: C_AsyncComplete/C_AsyncGetID/C_AsyncJoin → CKR_FUNCTION_NOT_SUPPORTED; C_GetFunctionStatus/C_CancelFunction → CKR_FUNCTION_NOT_PARALLEL; C_DigestKey/C_GetOperationState/C_SetOperationState → CKR_FUNCTION_NOT_SUPPORTED — all asserted three ways, matching the C++ suite's own honest-not-supported design for this category.

GapAes.justification: AES-ECB (RW3) and now AES-GCM (G1 gap-remediation, via the CK_GCM_PARAMS RW-P builder) both cased: one-shot round trip, FSM byte-equality against the one-shot, and real tag-tamper rejection. AES-CTR/CBC not separately cased — reachable via the same generic verb, CK_AES_CTR_PARAMS is pointer-free and needs no RW-P builder at all.

GapClassical.justification: Same as Classical — now has a real case_id (RSA-PKCS raw sign/verify + SignRecover/VerifyRecover).

GapEcdsaEddsa.justification: Same as ECDSA/EdDSA — now has real case_ids.

GapRsaCipher.justification: C_EncryptInit(RSA-OAEP)/C_Decrypt via the CK_RSA_PKCS_OAEP_PARAMS RW-P builder (G1 gap-remediation): real RSA-2048 keygen, OAEP encrypt/decrypt round trip, and OAEP's own re-randomization property (encrypting the same plaintext twice never reproduces the same ciphertext, both still decrypt correctly) — proven in-process and confirmed independently on both gRPC and REST (each transport's own randomized ciphertext decrypts correctly on that same transport).

GapRsaSign.justification: C_VerifySignatureInit/C_VerifySignature (pre-bound verify) proven to match plain C_Verify's own code; C_VerifySignatureUpdate/C_VerifySignatureFinal (the multipart continuation — an RW-T coverage-ledger audit finding, missed by RW6a's original sweep) proven to agree with the one-shot form on both a good and a tampered signature. C_SignRecoverInit/C_VerifyRecoverInit wired and reachable, proven via the real CKR_MECHANISM_INVALID they return for a non-RSA mechanism (this engine restricts Sign/VerifyRecover to RSA) — the RSA-positive recover round trip itself not cased. C_SignRecover/C_VerifyRecover wired, reached only via the negative path above.

HBSProtect.justification: Hash-based-signature (SLH-DSA/XMSS/HSS) sign/verify parity — split in G4 (2026-08-26) by keygen cost: V21a (SLH-DSA) is fast and runs in the routine suite; V21b (XMSS/HSS) is `#[ignore]`d (documented reason: XMSS keygen ~326s at this engine's smallest parameter set) rather than wired into the routine gate.

HybridKEM.justification: ECDH-as-KEM ‖ ML-KEM combined via CKM_CONCATENATE_BASE_AND_KEY — sender/receiver sides proven to agree on the same combined secret.

Init.justification: C_Initialize/C_Finalize are server-process bootstrap lifecycle (master plan §3 'Split' row) — no per-request network analogue; documented, not silently dropped.

KCV.justification: CKA_CHECK_VALUE read via the generic C_GetAttributeValue verb on a freshly generated AES key — proven present and non-empty (§4.11: computed on every secret-key creation). G3, 2026-08-26.

KEM.justification: C_EncapsulateKey/C_DecapsulateKey (v3.2 key-object form) — cross-transport shared-secret agreement proven, plus same-transport round trip and implicit-rejection on a tampered ciphertext.

KEMKcv.justification: Same attribute, on the shared-secret key an ML-KEM-768 C_DecapsulateKey produces — proven present and non-empty. G3, 2026-08-26.

KEMNeg.justification: The tampered-ciphertext sub-case proves ML-KEM's real implicit-rejection property (a corrupted ciphertext decapsulates to a different, deterministic-pseudorandom secret, never an error code).

KEMValueLen.justification: The case asserts the real ML-KEM-768 ciphertext length (1088 bytes) and shared-secret length (32 bytes).

KMAC.justification: CKM_KMAC_128, absent (default) params — per §0's correction, this needs no native engine wrapper; the generic sign path already dispatches it. Real MAC produced over a generic-secret key. G3, 2026-08-26.

KcvTemplate.justification: Same attribute, on a key produced via C_UnwrapKey (template form) rather than C_GenerateKey — proven present and non-empty. G3, 2026-08-26.

MechFlags.justification: Same as Discovery/G2MechTable — C_GetMechanismInfo's flags field is part of the parity assertion.

MsgCrypt.justification: C_MessageEncryptInit/C_EncryptMessage/C_EncryptMessageBegin/C_EncryptMessageNext/C_MessageEncryptFinal and the C_*Decrypt* equivalents (C_MessageDecryptInit/C_DecryptMessage/C_DecryptMessageBegin/C_DecryptMessageNext/C_MessageDecryptFinal) — one-shot + Begin/Next multipart, including the GcmMessageParams RW-P variant with real tag OUT/IN semantics and generated-IV round trip.

MultiPart.justification: C_DigestUpdate/C_DigestFinal, C_SignUpdate/C_SignFinal, C_VerifyInit/C_Verify/C_VerifyUpdate/C_VerifyFinal, C_EncryptUpdate/C_EncryptFinal, C_DecryptInit/C_DecryptUpdate/C_DecryptFinal — Init/Update/Final FSMs, including CKR_OPERATION_ACTIVE mixing guards.

MultiPart_ECDSA.justification: CKM_ECDSA_SHA256 (hash-combined, genuinely streamable — unlike bare CKM_ECDSA's single-part-only raw form) Update/Final FSM proven byte-identical to the one-shot Sign, plus a real Verify of the result. G3, 2026-08-26.

MultiPart_EdDSA.justification: Plain CKM_EDDSA Update/Final FSM proven byte-identical to the one-shot Sign (the engine buffers the message internally across Update calls; pure Ed25519 is deterministic so this equality is a real, meaningful assertion, not a coincidence), plus a real Verify of the result. G3, 2026-08-26.

Negative.justification: Every negative-path case across V1-V21 captures its expected CKR from an in-process control, never a hardcoded literal.

PQKeyBytes.justification: PQ (ML-DSA) public/private key attribute reads via the same generic C_GetAttributeValue path.

Profile.justification: The engine's built-in CKO_PROFILE objects, found via C_FindObjectsInit/C_FindObjects and read via C_GetAttributeValue (CKA_PROFILE_ID) — pure existing-verb composition, proven to return at least one real profile object. G3, 2026-08-26.

RawEncoding.justification: CKA_EC_POINT read via the generic C_GetAttributeValue verb on a freshly generated EC public key — proven present and non-empty. G3, 2026-08-26.

SHA-3.justification: Same as G-DA-X — CKM_SHA3_256 digest, one-shot and FSM proven to agree. G3, 2026-08-26.

SLHDSA.justification: SLH-DSA-SHA2 and SLH-DSA-SHAKE parameter sets, both cased. Split into its own V21a case in G4 (2026-08-26, was previously sharing V21's `#[ignore]` mark with XMSS/HSS purely for shared session/transport setup) — SLH-DSA-128S keygen is fast, so this now runs in the routine suite, not `#[ignore]`d.

Session.justification: C_OpenSession/C_CloseSession/C_Login/C_Logout/C_GetSessionInfo/C_LoginUser/C_SessionCancel/C_CloseAllSessions, plus the destructive-gated C_InitToken/C_InitPIN/C_SetPIN — the RPC half of the master plan §3 'Init, Session → Split' row. C_GetSessionValidationFlags (an RW-T audit finding) proven to return the real, honest empty flag set (this engine performs no FIPS/validation-authority checks) plus the real CKR_ARGUMENTS_BAD on an undefined type. C_CloseAllSessions's real destructive path (closing this process's shared bootstrap session) is proven only in the core crate's serialized admin_info_and_slot_functions_are_real (not referenced by case_id here since it wasn't the plan's chosen exemplar), not in the parallel acceptance suite — see the RW6a execution log entry for why.

WrapTemplate.justification: C_UnwrapKey's template form, including the real CKR_KEY_UNEXTRACTABLE negative.

XMSS.justification: Split into its own V21b case in G4 (2026-08-26, was V21 combined with SLH-DSA). `#[ignore]`d — measured ~326s for the whole sweep at this engine's smallest single-tree parameter set (height 10, no smaller option exists per v3.2 §6.66.6).

XmssParamSet.justification: Same case as XMSS (V21b) — only the default parameter set (CKP_XMSS_SHA2_10_256) exercised; other XMSS/XMSSMT parameter sets reachable via the same generic C_GenerateKeyPair template but not cased (would each cost more Merkle-tree keygen time).

SplitKey.justification: VENDOR EXTENSION (not a pkcs11f.h category; not in cpp_compliance_report.json). SplitKey/JoinKey RPCs added in G2 gap-remediation (2026-08-26), wrapping softhsmrustv3::native::split/join directly (no CKM_PQCTODAY_SPLIT_KEY C_* dispatch arm exists to go through, unlike every other row in this ledger). method/polynomial use the KMIP 3.0 §11.54/§11.55 enumeration codepoints verbatim. Proven: XOR split→join round trip recovering the original secret; GF(2^8) 5-part/3-threshold split with a JOIN using only a 3-of-5 subset (the actual threshold property, not just a full-set round trip); a below-threshold join rejected with the real CKR_ARGUMENTS_BAD; XOR's parts==threshold constraint (§13.1) rejected when violated; undefined method/polynomial wire codes rejected before any engine call.
